Presenting someone else’s work or ideas as your own. This includes representing the work of another student or institution as your own, or presenting work generated by, but unattributed to Artificial Intelligence (AI).
This is where a third party (including a person or AI) completes work on your behalf which you then submit as your own unaided work.
Unacceptable use of AI may fall into any of the definitions of Academic Misconduct listed in this document.
Verbatim copying or insertion of another’s work without appropriate acknowledgement. This includes published or unpublished work and material freely available in electronic form or generated by AI.
The fabrication of references or a bibliography.

Possession of any unauthorised material in an examination room, whether written, printed or electronically stored, unless expressly permitted by the regulations for the module or in-course assessment.
offences.anchor: Cheating in examinations (or other formal assessment)

offences.quote: Knowingly permitting another student to copy all or part of your work and allowing them to submit that work as their own unaided work.
Attempting to obtain special consideration by offering or receiving inducements or favours; that is, bribery.
Submitting the same (or substantially the same) work that you have already submitted for another assessment, when this is not permitted.

liability.quote: This definition applies whether or not intent can be proven. The University does not distinguish between intentional and unintentional misconduct.
the intent to deceive in order to gain academic advantage
plagiarism, where this is identified as resulting from a lack of understanding

detection.quote: An oral investigation or ‘viva’. This may be used where there is reasonable doubt that your submission is your own work.
detection.anchor: Stage 2 – Investigation and Establishing a Case

detection.quote: Where the marker of a piece of assessed work suspects Academic Misconduct has occurred, they will immediately advise the module leader, misconduct lead or equivalent.

process.quote: you will be invited to an informal meeting with your tutor or lecturer.
Suspected misconduct in a formal examination is considered a Grave offence and, in all cases, will be referred directly to an Academic Misconduct Panel.
process.anchor: 6. How we deal with Academic Misconduct in a timed examination

process.quote: an investigation will take place to determine whether academic misconduct has occurred.
At the meeting, the Chair will explain their suspicions and provide a copy of the evidence. You will then have the opportunity to respond to the allegations.
If you do not accept the local outcome agreed by the Head of Department, you have the right to present your case in person before an Academic Misconduct Panel.
process.anchor: 7. Student requests for an Academic Misconduct Panel

process.quote: If you do not attend the departmental meeting, it may proceed in your absence.
You have the right to be accompanied to this meeting by a friend.
You have the right to appeal the outcome of an Academic Misconduct Panel, however your appeal must meet one or more of the University’s grounds for appeal.
You will receive written notice of the Panel meeting at least 10 working days before it takes place.
The meeting will be documented, and a record kept by a note taker.

outcomes.quote: All outcomes that do not lead to a student’s withdrawal from the University must include a prescribed educational element around academic integrity.
Upon resubmission you will be capped at the pass mark for the whole module
(S4) You will be deemed to have failed in all assessments for the module/unit of a course.
If you refuse or fail to resubmit the element(s) of work as requested, a mark of zero will be awarded for the whole module.
If you are failed in a module due to Academic Misconduct, you will normally have the right to a standard reassessment, as detailed in the Academic Regulations
If evidence of Academic Misconduct becomes available after an Assessment or Award Board decision, that Board has the authority to reconsider its original decision.
Whether an offence is a first or subsequent offence may impact how it is classified.
when deciding the severity of the misconduct and appropriate sanction, panel members will consider the circumstances surrounding the case.

proven Academic Misconduct may bring into question your fitness to practise in your chosen profession. In such cases, we may invoke the University’s Fitness to Practise Procedures and/or report the activity to the relevant external body as appropriate in the circumstances.

definitions.quote: We define academic misconduct as activity which is likely to have the effect of gaining an academic advantage by the use of unfair and/or unacceptable methods.
